title: STORYFORGE II‚ AI PIXEL-ART VISUAL OVERHAUL TO MATCH THE REFERENCE
description:
# STORYFORGE II ‚AI PIXEL-ART VISUAL OVERHAUL TO MATCH THE REFERENCE

## 0. Starting point
Work from the code in the project checkout as it is now. Earlier work that was never
merged (old case branches, anything under .devion/worktrees) is abandoned: do not read
it, merge it or copy from it. Where something is missing, build it fresh.
Already in place and to be kept: React shell, Phaser 3.90 host, data-driven scene
builder, content schema, asset manifest, game store, Story Panel, contribution dialog.
The art is placeholder: every asset is a tiny flat SVG. This goal replaces the look.

Reference image: game/docs/reference/storyforge-ui-reference.png. Open it before
planning and before judging. Section 2 describes it in words.

## 1. Hard constraints
- Phaser stays on 3.90.x. React, TypeScript, Vite, Tailwind, Radix, Zustand stay.
- Keep the Go API contracts and the contribution flow. No mock data in place of real calls.
- Scene content stays data-driven: no object, position or asset hardcoded in a scene class.
- All art is raster pixel art generated inside the repo from source data by a
  deterministic script. No downloaded art, no image services, no CDN links.
- One native scene resolution of 480x270, scaled by whole numbers only, nearest-neighbour.
- One shared palette of at most 48 colours, defined once and used by art and UI.
- Fonts are bundled through npm packages, not loaded from a URL.

## 2. Visual target
A cosy night-time bedroom in rich pixel art with a framed adventure-game interface.
- Mood: deep indigo and plum shadows, warm wood, brass and gold trim, parchment cream.
  Cool moonlight from the window against warm lamp light on the desk.
- Header bar, wood with brass corners: gold "STORYFORGE" logo, a plaque with the world
  name, a round pill with a status dot and the round id, the countdown, a gold primary
  button "+ SUGGEST WHAT HAPPENS NEXT", sound and settings icons.
- Game area, about three quarters of the width: striped wallpaper over wood wainscot,
  plank floor, window with curtains and a crescent moon, desk with an old computer,
  lamp and plant, wall poster, bookshelf with books and a globe, bed with a patterned
  blanket, door with light under it, rug, and the boy in a blue hoodie.
- Selected object: a name plate above it ("OLD BOOKSHELF") with its actions as small
  buttons beneath (INSPECT, SEARCH, PUSH) and a hand cursor.
- Right panel in the same frame style: chapter title, a parchment card with the
  speaker's portrait, name and line, the available choices as a list, a 3x2 inventory
  grid with item icons and names, and a short event log.

## 3. Deliverables
3.1 Art pipeline. Sprites are authored as palette-indexed pixel grids in source files.
    A script turns them into PNG sprite sheets and updates the manifest. The drawing
    code is pure functions, so tests can check size, frame count and palette use.
3.2 Room art. Layered PNGs for wall, wainscot, floor, window with night sky, and each
    piece of furniture and each object in section 2, with shading and outlines, drawn
    at native scale. Every placeholder SVG of the room is replaced and removed.
3.3 Character. The boy as a 32x48 sprite with idle (4 frames), walk (6) and interact
    (4) animations, plus a 32x32 portrait for the dialogue card.
3.4 Light and atmosphere. Moonlight shaft, lamp glow, light under the door, drifting
    dust and a soft vignette, built from scene content and placed on the effects layer.
3.5 Interface frame kit. Nine-slice frames for bar, panel, plaque, parchment card,
    inventory slot and buttons (normal, hover, pressed, disabled), a hand cursor, and
    design tokens for colour, spacing and type shared by every component.
3.6 Header rebuilt on the kit, showing live round id, status and countdown.
3.7 Story panel rebuilt on the kit: chapter title, dialogue card with portrait,
    choices, inventory grid with item icons, event log. It scrolls on its own.
3.8 Object interaction in the scene: hover highlight, name plate, action buttons
    anchored to the object, driven by the object's content definition.
3.9 Behaviour carried over from the last goal:
    - Game actions play the character's interact animation and scene changes fade.
    - A scene change to an empty or unknown scene is ignored.
    - Every interactive object can be reached and used by keyboard and screen reader,
      with labels from the same game state. The unused hotspot-over-image path is removed.
3.10 The game screen uses all of the above: no placeholder art or old styling remains.

## 4. Skills this work needs
Propose agents whose skills are the techniques below, written as reusable know-how:
- Pixel-art sprite authoring: silhouettes, outlines, shading with colour ramps, dithering.
- Limited-palette design: building ramps and keeping warm and cool light consistent.
- Sprite-sheet layout and frame animation timing.
- Pixel-perfect rendering: whole-number scaling, nearest-neighbour, device pixel ratio.
- Layered 2D lighting and particles in a scene engine.
- Nine-slice interface frames and state variants.
- Design tokens and component styling in a utility-CSS setup.
- Anchoring DOM overlays to objects in a canvas scene.
- Accessible alternatives for canvas content.
- Generating image files from data with deterministic, testable code.

## 5. Done when
- Every asset in the manifest is a generated PNG at its declared size using only the
  shared palette, and no placeholder SVG is referenced.
- The game screen shows the room, the boy, the lighting and the framed interface as
  section 2 describes, with the header, panel and object interaction working on real data.
- Section 3.9 behaviour works and is covered by unit tests.
- Layout holds from 1280x720 up, and the panel becomes a bottom drawer on narrow screens.

## 6. Out of scope
New rooms, new story content, backend changes, audio, deployment, repository clean-up.

agents.name: pixel-artisan
agents.role: Act agent that authors palette-indexed pixel art sources and the deterministic script that turns them into PNG sprite sheets and manifest entries.
agents.summary: Owns the shared palette (48 colours or fewer), the room, furniture, object, character, portrait, cursor and UI-frame art sources, and the generator script. Drawing code is pure functions so Verify can test size, frame count and palette use. Every placeholder SVG is replaced and removed.

skills.name: pixel-art-sprite-authoring
skills.description: Author small raster sprites as palette-indexed grids with clear silhouettes, outlines, ramp shading and selective dithering.

guide.when_to_use: Creating characters, props, tiles or icons from source data at native resolution, where readability at tiny sizes matters.
practices: Store each sprite as a grid of palette indices, with one index reserved for transparent.
Block the silhouette first and check that it reads in a single flat colour.
Add a darker outline, or a selective outline tinted by the neighbouring colour.
Shade with 3 to 5 step colour ramps and one fixed light direction for the whole set.
Use dithering only on large gradients, and use clean pixel clusters elsewhere.
Build animation frames from a shared base with small offsets so volume and the foot anchor stay stable.
pitfalls: Single-pixel noise clutters the sprite, so merge it into clusters.
Pillow shading, where the light comes from the middle, flattens the form, so keep one light direction.
Mixed pixel scales break the style, so draw everything at the same native resolution.
Jittering anchor points between frames makes the sprite shake, so fix the pivot.
checks: The sprite is recognisable as a flat silhouette.
Every pixel index resolves to a palette entry.
Frame dimensions are identical across an animation.

skills.name: limited-palette-ramp-design
skills.description: Build a small shared colour palette from hue-shifted ramps so warm and cool lighting stay consistent across art and interface.

guide.when_to_use: Defining or extending a colour set with a hard cap, shared by artwork and UI, for a scene with two light temperatures.
practices: Split the budget into ramps of 3 to 6 colours per material family, plus a few neutrals.
Shift hue toward warm in highlights and toward cool or violet in shadows.
Reserve separate warm and cool ramps for light sources and tint lit surfaces from them.
Define the palette once as data and generate stylesheet tokens from the same source.
Verify contrast of text against its background inside the palette.
pitfalls: Adding one-off colours breaks the cap, so extend a ramp instead.
Pure-black outlines look harsh, so use a very dark tinted colour.
Ramps with evenly spaced lightness look dull, so vary the steps.
checks: The unique colour count is at or below the cap.
Art and UI import the same palette file.
Text and background pairs meet the contrast target.

skills.name: deterministic-image-generation
skills.description: Generate image files from source data with pure functions and a byte-stable encoder so outputs are reproducible and unit testable.

guide.when_to_use: Building assets in a build step instead of editing binaries by hand, or whenever generated files are committed.
practices: Keep rendering as pure functions from data to a pixel buffer with no I/O or clock.
Isolate the PNG encoding and file writing in a thin wrapper.
Fix the compression settings and strip metadata and timestamps so identical input gives identical bytes.
Update the asset manifest from the generator output, not by hand.
Expose dimensions, frame count and colour use as functions that tests can call.
pitfalls: Randomness without a fixed seed changes the output between runs, so use a seeded generator.
Mixing disk access into the drawing code makes it untestable, so inject the writer.
Iterating over files in unsorted order changes the manifest, so sort the keys.
checks: Running the generator twice gives byte-identical files.
A test can verify the size and palette of each output without touching the disk.

agents.name: lumen-renderer
agents.role: Act agent for the canvas rendering layer: pixel-perfect scaling, layered scene composition, lighting and particles.
agents.summary: Configures the Phaser 3.90 host for one 480x270 native resolution with whole-number nearest-neighbour scaling. Builds the moonlight shaft, lamp glow, door light, dust and vignette from scene content on the effects layer. Wires the character animations and interact-triggered fades.

skills.name: pixel-perfect-canvas-scaling
skills.description: Render a fixed low-resolution canvas at whole-number scale with nearest-neighbour sampling that accounts for device pixel ratio.

guide.when_to_use: Showing low-resolution pixel graphics in a resizable container without blur or uneven pixels.
practices: Fix one native resolution and compute the scale as the floor of the available size divided by native size.
Centre the canvas and letterbox the remainder.
Set the renderer to pixelArt and nearest filtering, and disable antialiasing and rounding drift.
Fold device pixel ratio into the scale so one image pixel maps to a whole number of device pixels.
Convert pointer coordinates back through the same scale.
pitfalls: CSS fractional scaling blurs pixels, so use integer factors.
Smoothing left on in some texture paths blurs only some sprites, so set filtering globally.
Sub-pixel camera or sprite positions shimmer, so round positions.
checks: The scale function always returns an integer of at least 1.
Screenshots at several window sizes show crisp edges.

skills.name: layered-2d-lighting-particles
skills.description: Compose cheap 2D lighting and ambient particles as blended sprite layers over a scene.

guide.when_to_use: Adding mood lighting, glows, shafts, vignettes and drifting motes to a 2D engine without a full lighting system.
practices: Draw glows and shafts as pre-baked soft sprites with additive or screen blending on a layer above the world.
Draw the vignette as one multiply-blended overlay.
Use a particle emitter with a low count, slow speed, alpha fade and a bounded zone.
Add a slow sine flicker or pulse to the intensity of each light.
Derive light positions and colours from the content data.
pitfalls: Too many full-screen blended layers hurt fill rate, so merge them where possible.
Lights tinted outside the palette break the style, so use palette colours.
Particles that never die leak memory, so give each a lifespan.
checks: Removing the effects layer leaves a valid scene.
Particle counts stay bounded over time.

agents.name: frame-smith
agents.role: Act agent for the framed interface: frame kit, design tokens, header and story panel.
agents.summary: Builds nine-slice frames with state variants and shared tokens for colour, spacing and type. Rebuilds the header and story panel on the kit using live store data. The panel scrolls independently and becomes a bottom drawer on narrow screens. Fonts come from npm packages.

skills.name: nine-slice-frame-kit
skills.description: Build resizable bordered interface frames from a single small image using nine-slice scaling with state variants.

guide.when_to_use: Skinning panels, buttons and plaques with bitmap art that must stretch without distorting its corners.
practices: Cut each frame into fixed corners, stretched edges and a stretched or tiled centre, and record the slice insets.
Apply the image with border-image or a nine-slice component, with pixelated rendering and whole-pixel insets.
Define normal, hover, pressed and disabled variants as sibling images with identical slice geometry.
Keep the content padding at least as large as the border insets.
pitfalls: Fractional insets blur the borders, so use integers.
Variants with different borders make content jump, so keep the geometry identical.
Stretching a patterned centre looks wrong, so tile it or use a flat fill.
checks: Resizing the frame leaves the corners unchanged.
Every variant uses the same insets.

skills.name: design-tokens-utility-css
skills.description: Define colour, spacing and type tokens once and expose them to a utility-CSS framework and components.

guide.when_to_use: Keeping many components visually consistent in a Tailwind-style setup or a bespoke theme.
practices: Keep tokens as the single source, as CSS variables or a theme config, with semantic names such as surface and accent.
Map the tokens into the utility framework theme so classes use them directly.
Build components on semantic tokens instead of raw values.
Load fonts from packages and declare a font-display and a fallback stack.
Disable image smoothing on bitmap-skinned elements.
pitfalls: Hex values hardcoded in components drift from the tokens, so lint for them.
Token names that describe a colour instead of a role make themes hard to change.
Fonts loaded from remote hosts break offline use, so bundle them.
checks: Searching component files finds no raw colour values.
Changing one token updates every consumer.

agents.name: anchor-weaver
agents.role: Act agent that links the canvas scene to the DOM: object overlays, action buttons and accessible alternatives.
agents.summary: Builds hover highlight, name plate and action buttons anchored to the selected object from its content definition. Adds keyboard and screen-reader access with labels from game state. Removes the hotspot-over-image path. Ignores scene changes to empty or unknown scenes.

skills.name: dom-overlay-canvas-anchoring
skills.description: Position DOM elements over canvas objects by converting world coordinates to screen coordinates.

guide.when_to_use: Showing labels, menus or buttons attached to objects inside a canvas scene.
practices: Convert object bounds to screen pixels using the canvas bounding rect, the display scale and the camera offset.
Publish the anchor rectangle through a typed event or store, and recompute it on resize, camera change and object movement.
Render the overlay in a positioned layer above the canvas and flip it near the edges.
Remove the anchor when the selection clears.
pitfalls: Stale rectangles after resize misplace the overlay, so subscribe to resize.
An overlay that captures pointer events blocks the canvas, so limit pointer events to its controls.
Updating on every frame wastes work, so update only on change.
checks: The overlay stays attached through a resize.
Edge cases keep the overlay inside the viewport.

skills.name: canvas-accessible-mirror
skills.description: Expose canvas-only interactive content through a parallel DOM of focusable, labelled controls.

guide.when_to_use: Making game or canvas content usable by keyboard and screen readers.
practices: Render a visually hidden list of buttons, one per interactive item, with labels from the same state as the canvas.
Keep focus and hover in sync between the canvas and the DOM, and show a focus ring on the canvas object.
Announce changes through a polite live region.
Remove duplicated or obsolete pointer-only paths.
pitfalls: Labels hardcoded apart from the state go stale, so derive them from state.
Hidden with display none removes the items from the accessibility tree, so use a visually-hidden style.
Focus lost on re-render, so use stable keys.
checks: All interactive objects are reachable by Tab.
The label text matches the on-screen name.

agents.name: pixel-verify
agents.role: Verify agent that tests the generators, pure drawing functions, store behaviour and layout contracts with all dependencies mocked.
agents.summary: Writes unit tests for the palette cap, sprite sizes, frame counts, manifest PNG references, ignoring scene changes to empty or unknown scenes, transition fades, interact animation triggers, keyboard access and drawer layout rules. It never starts a browser or the app.

skills.name: generated-image-assertions
skills.description: Assert properties of generated raster images in unit tests by decoding bytes or inspecting pixel buffers.

guide.when_to_use: Testing code that produces images, sprite sheets or atlases without opening a viewer.
practices: Test pure drawing functions on in-memory buffers and compare width, height and frame count.
Collect the set of unique colours and assert it is a subset of the allowed palette.
Decode the PNG header to check the dimensions of the written files.
Compare the output of two runs to prove determinism.
Cross-check every manifest entry against an existing file and its declared size.
pitfalls: Snapshot comparisons of whole binaries are brittle, so assert properties instead.
Alpha edge pixels may add unexpected colours, so ignore fully transparent pixels.
checks: A deliberately wrong palette colour makes the test fail.
Tests run without touching the real output directory.

nodes.title: Build the palette and pixel-art generation pipeline
nodes.criteria: A single palette module defines at most 48 colours and exports them for the art script, the UI tokens and Tailwind. The game constants become 480x270 and computeZoom keeps returning whole numbers (min 1, using the device pixel ratio). Phaser renders with pixelArt true and nearest-neighbour. Sprites are authored as palette-indexed grids in source files. Pure functions turn a grid into RGBA pixels and into a sprite sheet, and a deterministic script writes PNGs and updates the asset manifest with the real size, frame width and height, and frame count. Unit tests check output size, frame count, palette-only colours and identical bytes on repeated runs.

children.title: Define the shared palette and 480x270 render constants
children.criteria: One palette file lists at most 48 hex colours in named warm and cool ramps and is exported as constants and as Tailwind colours. config.ts uses 480x270, and computeZoom is covered by tests for whole-number zoom at several window sizes and DPR values. Existing tests that assume 640x360 are updated.

children.title: Write pure grid-to-pixels and sprite-sheet functions
children.criteria: Pure functions convert a palette-indexed grid to RGBA and lay frames out into a sheet. Unit tests check width, height, frame count, that every pixel colour is in the palette, and that an out-of-range index throws.

children.title: Add the PNG generation script and manifest update
children.criteria: A script under scripts/ reads the grid sources, encodes PNGs deterministically with no timestamps and writes them to public/assets. It rewrites manifest entries with path, size and frame data. Unit tests check that two runs give identical bytes and that manifest sizes match the generated PNG headers. An npm script is added for it.

children.title: In game/frontend/scripts/generateArt.ts, defaultArtPaths resolves…
children.criteria: Technical: In game/frontend/scripts/generateArt.ts, defaultArtPaths resolves assetsRoot to <scriptDir>/../public/assets (game/frontend/public/assets). The app's manifest is game/public/assets/worlds/the-boys-room/manifest.json, imported by src/runtime/content.ts. Change defaultArtPaths to resolve assetsRoot as <scriptDir>/../../public/assets, with manifestPath under it at worlds/the-boys-room/manifest.json. Update the defaultArtPaths test in game/frontend/tests/generateArtScript.test.ts to expect /repo/game/public/assets and /repo/game/public/assets/worlds/the-boys-room/manifest.json.

nodes.title: Replace the room and character art
nodes.criteria: The grid sources for the room layers (wall, wainscot, floor, window with night sky, desk, old computer, lamp, plant, poster, bookshelf with books and globe, bed with patterned blanket, door, rug, inventory item icons) and the boy are authored, with outlines and ramp shading, at native scale. The boy is a 32x48 sheet with idle 4, walk 6 and interact 4 frames, plus a 32x32 portrait. The generated PNGs replace every room SVG, and the world content file and manifest reference only PNGs. The old SVGs are deleted. BootScene loads and registers the new animations by frame counts from the manifest. A manifest test checks that each asset is a PNG at its declared size using only palette colours, and that no .svg is referenced.
covers: 5 Every asset is a generated PNG using only the shared palette

children.title: Author the room shell and furniture grids
children.criteria: Source grids for wall, wainscot, floor, window with night sky, desk, computer, lamp, plant, poster, bookshelf with books and globe, bed, door and rug exist at their declared sizes. Tests check size and palette use for each.

children.title: Author the boy sheet and portrait
children.criteria: A 32x48 sheet with idle (4), walk (6) and interact (4) frames and a 32x32 portrait are generated. The manifest declares the animations with frame ranges and rates. Tests check frame counts and size.

children.title: Switch content and manifest to the PNGs and remove the SVGs
children.criteria: The world scene content and manifest reference only the new PNG ids. BootScene preloads them with no fallback texture used. All placeholder SVGs under public/assets, including bedroom.svg, are deleted. Tests assert that no .svg path remains in the manifest or content and that BootScene tests still pass.

nodes.title: Add lighting and atmosphere effects
nodes.criteria: Moonlight shaft, lamp glow, light under the door, drifting dust and a soft vignette are built by buildEffects from the scene content effect definitions. They are placed on the effects layer in layers.ts and use palette colours. The dust particles use the generated dust sprite. Phaser effects created from content are destroyed on scene shutdown. Unit tests with a mocked render context check that each effect type is created from the content, layer depth is used, and destroy is called.

nodes.title: Build the interface frame kit and design tokens
nodes.criteria: Design tokens for colour (from the palette), spacing and type are defined once and exposed as CSS variables and Tailwind theme values. Pixel fonts are installed through npm @fontsource packages and imported locally. Nine-slice frame PNGs for bar, panel, plaque, parchment card, inventory slot and buttons (normal, hover, pressed, disabled) and a hand cursor are generated by the pipeline. React components or utility classes apply them with border-image or equivalent, with image-rendering: pixelated, and a button shows all four states. The old panel-frame, sound and pointer SVGs are removed. Unit tests check token values come from the palette, that the Tailwind config exposes the tokens, and that button state classes render.

nodes.title: Rebuild the header and the story panel on the kit
nodes.criteria: HeaderOverlay is rebuilt as a wood bar with brass corners: gold STORYFORGE logo, world-name plaque, round pill with a status dot and the live round id, the Countdown, a gold + SUGGEST WHAT HAPPENS NEXT button that opens the contribution dialog, and sound and settings icons wired to uiStore. StoryPanel is rebuilt in the panel frame: chapter title, parchment dialogue card with the 32x32 portrait, speaker name and line, the choices list, a 3x2 inventory grid with icons and names from game state, and an event log. It scrolls on its own. Everything reads real store and API data. Existing header, story, countdown and contribution tests are updated and new tests cover each region and each status.
covers: 2 Visual target (header bar and right panel)

children.title: Rebuild HeaderOverlay on the kit
children.criteria: The header shows the logo, plaque, status pill with dot and round id, countdown, gold suggest button and sound and settings icons. Tests cover the loading, error and retry states, and that the suggest button opens the contribution dialog.

children.title: Rebuild StoryPanel on the kit
children.criteria: The panel shows chapter title, dialogue card with portrait, choices, a 3x2 inventory grid with icons and names, and an event log, with its own overflow scroll. Tests cover empty inventory slots, choice selection and log rendering from game state.

nodes.title: Add in-scene object interaction and remove the hotspot path
nodes.criteria: Hovering or focusing an object in the Phaser scene highlights it, shows a name plate above it ('OLD BOOKSHELF') and action buttons beneath it (INSPECT, SEARCH, PUSH), anchored to the object's screen position. The labels and actions come from the object's content definition and are used through the existing objectClick and action flow. The anchor position is a pure function of the object's native position, the scale, the canvas offset and DPR, and it is recomputed on resize. The hand cursor is used on interactive objects. Every object and its actions is reachable by Tab, arrows, Enter and Space, with a screen-reader live region and labels read from the same game state. SceneView, HOTSPOTS and ASSET_PATHS are deleted. Tests cover the anchor maths, the action list from content, the keyboard flow and the ARIA labels.
covers: 3.9 Every interactive object can be reached by keyboard and screen reader
3.9 The unused hotspot-over-image path is removed

nodes.title: Integrate the game screen, behaviours and responsive layout
nodes.criteria: GameLayout uses the new header, scene at 480x270 with whole-number scale, and story panel, with about three quarters of the width for the game area and the rest for the panel. Layout holds from 1280x720 up. Below the narrow breakpoint the panel is a bottom drawer driven by uiStore. Game actions emit playAnimation so the boy plays the interact animation, scene changes fade via transitionTo, and a transition to an empty or unknown scene id is ignored. Old placeholder styling in styles.css is removed. Unit tests cover the layout at wide and narrow widths, the drawer toggle, the interact animation on an action, the fade on a valid scene change, and the ignored empty or unknown scene.
covers: 3.9 Game actions play the interact animation and scene changes fade
3.9 A scene change to an empty or unknown scene is ignored
3.10 Game screen uses all of the above
5 Layout holds from 1280x720 up, bottom drawer on narrow screens
5 Section 3.9 behaviour covered by unit tests

constraints: Phaser stays on 3.90.x (the current ~3.90.0 pin and its guard tests stay). React, TypeScript, Vite, Tailwind, Radix and Zustand stay.
Keep the Go API contracts and the contribution flow. No mock data in place of real API calls.
Scene content stays data-driven: no object, position or asset id is hardcoded in a scene class.
All art is raster pixel art generated inside the repo from source data by a deterministic script. No downloaded art, no image services, no CDN links.
One native scene resolution of 480x270, scaled by whole numbers only, with nearest-neighbour sampling. The current 640x360 constants change to this.
One shared palette of at most 48 colours, defined once and used by both art and UI.
Fonts are bundled through npm packages, not loaded from a URL.
Out of scope: new rooms, new story content, backend changes, audio, deployment, repository clean-up.
Tests are unit tests with all dependencies mocked. Earlier unmerged work and anything under .devion/worktrees is not read or copied.
